methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses multiple complementary approaches: CD8-conditional STING/TOX knockout mice (Cd8cre x Sting1flox and Toxflox), multiple syngeneic tumor models (TC-1, MC38, B16F10, CT26), adoptive cell therapy in NSG hosts, human patient samples (n=123 cervical cancer paraffin tissues), bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, flow cytometry, multiplex immunofluorescence, lentiviral rescue (HMOX1 shRNA), and combination therapies with ICB, STING agonist, and cisplatin. Statistical treatment includes unpaired t-tests, ANOVA, Wilcoxon, Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, and data-driven cutoffs, but lacks formal multiplicity correction for the many parallel omics comparisons and pre-specified power calculations. Limitations are partially acknowledged (small n per mouse group: 4-5/arm), but the convergent genetic, pharmacologic, and patient validation provide strong mechanistic support.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is fundamentally preclinical (mouse models and cell lines), mapping to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is nonetheless substantial: it proposes engineered STING/TOX-deficient CD8+ T cells for adoptive cell therapy combined with checkpoint blockade, ties findings to human cervical cancer tissue (123 patients), and identifies lactate-MCT1-HO-1 as an actionable axis. The translational path is plausible and directly informs ACT/ICB combination strategies, though it is not yet practice-changing without first-in-human data.

reporting_quality.justification: As a preclinical animal study, ARRIVE is the applicable standard. The methods describe mouse strain origins, housing conditions, randomization by gender, ethical approvals (L102012022001Z and IRB G2022-133-01), group sizes, endpoints, and humane limits (tumor volume <=2000 mm^3). A Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced. Blinding is not explicitly described and sample-size justification is not provided. Data availability is strong: bulk RNA-seq in GSA (CRA011572), scRNA-seq in GSA-Human (HRA003358), and referenced public GEO dataset GSE162025, with primer/antibody lists in Supplementary Dataset 1.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper links STING and TOX into a positive regulatory loop that represses HO-1 and drives ferroptosis specifically in tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells, and identifies lactate as an upstream TME trigger. Prior literature separately addressed STING in T cells (Larkin 2017, Wu 2019), TOX in exhaustion (Khan 2019, Scott 2019), HO-1 in ferroptosis, and lactate's immunosuppressive role, but the integration into a STING-TOX-HO-1 axis coupling ferroptosis to immunotherapy resistance is a meaningful new synthesis. It is not first-in-class for any single component, but the mechanistic convergence and therapeutic implication (engineered T cell deficiency) represent a novel extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract, introduction, and methods are well organized and precise; technical density is appropriate for a mechanistic immunology paper. Methods sections are exhaustively detailed (cell lines, antibodies, dosing schedules, timepoints). Occasional grammatical lapses and complex compound figures (inferred from text) would need cleanup, but overall the manuscript reads as publication-ready in a leading mechanistic journal.

key_strengths: Convergent genetic (CD8-conditional STING/TOX knockouts), pharmacologic (H151, DMXAA, ADU-S100), and human-tissue (n=123 cervical cancer) evidence for the STING-TOX-HO-1 ferroptosis axis
Therapeutically actionable: engineered STING/TOX-deficient CD8+ T cells synergize with anti-PD-1/TIM-3, cisplatin, and STING agonist in multiple syngeneic models
Identifies lactate-MCT1 as an upstream TME trigger, linking metabolism to T cell ferroptosis and immunotherapy resistance
Deposition of bulk and single-cell RNA-seq in public repositories with accession numbers
key_concerns: Small per-group sample sizes (4-5 mice) and absence of explicit power or multiplicity-correction statements
Blinding and randomization for tumor measurements are not documented
Human data limited to IHC associations; no prospective or functional human validation beyond healthy-donor T cells
Mechanistic claim of a STING-TOX regulatory loop would benefit from ChIP/CUT&RUN evidence for direct co-regulation of HMOX1
chief_reviewer.rationale: A mechanistically rich, multi-model preclinical paper with clear translational implications for ACT and ICB combinations; top-tier plausible with minor revisions to bolster rigor reporting (blinding, power, multiplicity).
